51515127.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to TTR V30M mutant (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli by ITC assay
51515127.references_previous: Reference 91: Yokoyama, T.; Kishihara, M.; Mizuguchi, M. Repositioning of the anthelmintic drugs bithionol and triclabendazole as transthyretin amyloidogenesis inhibitors. J. Med. Chem. 2021, 64, 14344–14357.

original_paragraph.ITC Measurements: To reduce the concentration of DMSO in both the protein solution and the compound solution, we performed a reverse titration experiment, in which the compound solution (30 μM) was titrated with small injections of the protein solution (150 or 200 μM). The compound solution was placed in the cell, while the protein solution was placed in the syringe. The protein solution was dialyzed against 50 mM sodium phosphate and 50 mM NaCl at pH 7.5 before ITC measurements. After dialysis, DMSO was added to a final concentration of 0.3%. A compound solution containing 30 μM compound, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 50 mM NaCl, and 0.3% DMSO at pH 7.5 was prepared. All solutions were degassed by centrifugation (20,652 × g, 10 min) prior to use. ITC experiments were performed using a MicroCal iTC200 microcalorimeter (Malvern Instruments, Malvern, UK). The compound solution was titrated with a protein solution containing 150 or 200 μM V30M-TTR. The titrations consisted of 18 injections with 180 s delay between injections and 750 rpm stirring at 25 °C. The data were analyzed and plotted with SEDPHAT, GUSSI, and NITPIC (University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, Texas). The ITC curves were fitted assuming that the tetramer has two ligand-binding sites, which are identical and independent. The contribution of the heat of dilution was subtracted from the titration data before the curve fitting.
